candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record demonstrates the hallmark features of retropharyngeal calcific tendinitis: acute posterior neck pain with odynophagia, retropharyngeal soft-tissue swelling on lateral radiograph, calcification anterior to C1 arch, and CT showing calcification in the longus colli extending to the atlanto-odontoid joint. C001 names the same diagnostic entity with the standard anatomical qualifier (longus colli), which does not introduce any incompatible subtype or scope conflict.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Retropharyngeal calcific tendinitis with explicit longus colli muscle specification; the reference diagnosis 'retropharyngeal calcific tendinitis' is the same entity, as this condition is characteristically caused by calcium hydroxyapatite deposition in the longus colli tendon/muscle — the added anatomical detail is a harmless, clinically accurate alias.

case_quality_flags: Classic presentation of retropharyngeal calcific tendinitis; imaging findings are pathognomonic and fully support the reference diagnosis.
